seo.meta_title: Are Carl's Jr. and Hardee's the Same? What's Different
seo.meta_description: Carl's Jr. and Hardee's share an owner, a star logo and many burgers, but they started as separate chains. Why there are two names and how they differ.
seo.h1: Are Carl's Jr. and Hardee's the Same?
seo.primary_keyword: is carl's jr and hardee's the same

question: Are Carl's Jr. and Hardee's the Same?
quick_answer: Mostly, but not completely. Carl's Jr. and Hardee's have the same owner, CKE Restaurants, the same smiling star logo and many of the same charbroiled burgers, like the Famous Star. But they started as separate chains on opposite sides of the country, and they still use different names in different regions: Carl's Jr. in the West and Southwest, Hardee's in the Midwest and Southeast. Their menus differ a little too.
key_facts: Both owned by CKE Restaurants, based in Franklin, Tennessee
Carl's Jr. began in Los Angeles in 1941; Hardee's in North Carolina in 1960
CKE bought Hardee's in 1997 for $327 million
Same star logo and many shared burgers
Carl's Jr. is mainly in the West; Hardee's in the Midwest and Southeast

body.heading: Two chains, one owner
body.text: Carl's Jr. and Hardee's are owned by the same company, CKE Restaurants, which is based in Franklin, Tennessee. CKE stands for Carl Karcher Enterprises, after the founder of Carl's Jr. That shared ownership is why the two chains use the same smiling star logo, similar restaurant designs and many of the same menu items. Their websites even look almost identical.

body.heading: How Carl's Jr. started
body.text: Carl Karcher started with a hot dog stand in Los Angeles in 1941. His business grew into Carl's Drive-In Barbecue, and in 1956 he opened the first smaller restaurants called Carl's Jr., where the star logo first appeared. In 1964 he incorporated the business as Carl Karcher Enterprises, and Carl's Jr. grew across California and the West.

body.heading: How Hardee's started
body.text: Wilber Hardee opened the first Hardee's in Greenville, North Carolina, in 1960. The chain grew fast by opening in smaller towns that McDonald's and Burger King hadn't reached, and by the early 1990s it had more than 2,500 restaurants, making it one of the biggest burger chains in the country. By the late 1990s, though, it was struggling.

body.heading: Why there are still two names
body.text: In 1997, CKE bought Hardee's for $327 million to expand east. Instead of renaming Hardee's, CKE kept both brands, because Hardee's had strong loyalty in its home regions. Over the next years, Hardee's adopted the Carl's Jr. star logo and many Carl's Jr. burgers. Today the two rarely overlap: Carl's Jr. is mostly in the West and Southwest, and Hardee's is mostly in the Midwest and Southeast.

body.heading: What's actually different
body.text: The core burgers are largely the same, including the Famous Star and Super Star, and the two chains often launch the same new items. The biggest difference is breakfast: Hardee's is known for its Made from Scratch biscuits, baked by hand every morning, and while Carl's Jr. later added them in some markets, they are much more central at Hardee's. Prices, limited-time items and some names also vary between the two.

faqs.q: Are Carl's Jr. and Hardee's the same company?
faqs.a: Yes. Both are owned by CKE Restaurants.

faqs.q: Why do Carl's Jr. and Hardee's have different names?
faqs.a: They started as separate chains. When CKE bought Hardee's in 1997, it kept the Hardee's name because of its strong regional following.

faqs.q: Do Carl's Jr. and Hardee's have the same menu?
faqs.a: Mostly. They share many burgers, like the Famous Star, but Hardee's is better known for its scratch-made breakfast biscuits, and prices and some items differ.

faqs.q: Which came first, Carl's Jr. or Hardee's?
faqs.a: Carl's Jr. Carl Karcher started his business in Los Angeles in 1941. The first Hardee's opened in North Carolina in 1960.
